title: Genkaku Picasso
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Hikari 'Picasso' Hamura, a loner who draws constantly, survives an accident that kills his only friend Chiaki. Chiaki returns as an angel-like figure and tells him he will rot and die unless he helps the people around him; he does so by drawing classmates' troubles and entering the pictures to understand them. Three volumes of episodic teen problems, from shyness to gender identity and family trauma.
life_message: Paying attention to other people's hidden pain, and helping them, is what makes a life worth living.

content.note: Slight violence (SLJ review); an accident kills Chiaki.
Hikari's body begins to rot if he fails to help; surreal hallucination scenes (MU Hallucination/s); death of a friend.
Mild, mostly artistic nudity and teen talk about sex (SLJ); a father uses his daughter as a model for fetish photos, clothed and not pornographic (SLJ), framed as a problem to resolve.
Childhood trauma, gender identity distress and loneliness worked through (SLJ review; MU Gender Identity Disorder, Mind Break); resolved toward acceptance.
Nothing risky noted; Hikari described as a bit of a pervert (SLJ).

dominant: Empathy and service to others; art as a path to understanding; accepting identity

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts are resolved by understanding, not confrontation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters are helped to be themselves.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Classmates rather than kin form the community helped.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Hikari, a social outsider, helps peers as an equal.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: An angel-like friend frames a largely secular school story.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Self-acceptance and emotional expression are the goal.

folkways.japan: Classroom social pressure and quiet, unspoken suffering among teens reflect Japanese norms of reserve and group conformity.

delivery.evidence: SLJ praises sensitive, realistic handling and humor; no moralizing noted. Each episode resolves one classmate's problem.
delivery.note: Each episode carries its point through one character's hidden problem and its resolution.

winners_losers: Hikari and his classmates win by opening up; the story sympathizes with outsiders, including a transgender classmate.
